mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or when FEDFUNDS rises but inflation expectations also rise sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth rebounds above trend within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered periods, or unemployment falls below 4% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months with YoY change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds above trend within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall >0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation expectations rise despite falling CPI and rates.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation (>0.7) between retail sales (RSAFS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past six months signals a breakdown of the typical negative demand-labor relationship, implying structural demand weakness that persists and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation reverts to the historical negative range within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable PAYEMS and falling UNRATE) above 63% for four consecutive months signals increased labor supply without corresponding job growth, which suppresses wage inflation and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls while PAYEMS rises, and participation implied > 63% for 4 months
regime_hint: labor supply expansion without job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or unemployment rises sharply despite participation increase.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) of more than 10% over six months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or housing starts decline sharply within the next quarter.
